title: Small state, strong farming presence
finding: Agriculture makes up 9.1% of Tasmania’s businesses, versus 4.9% in NSW.
note: Colour shows a share of actively trading businesses, not land area or employment. Main-state allocation; class-cell sums are approximate.

title: NSW has the largest business count
finding: NSW has 45,163 agriculture businesses; Tasmania has 4,015.
note: Circle area is proportional to business count. Points represent state totals, not farm locations. Unknown/other geography is excluded from maps.

title: Fewer registered dairy farms
finding: Registered dairy farms fell 44.3%, from 6,770 to 3,772.
note: This is a dairy-only series, not a count of all farms. The financial year runs July–June; 2024–25 is provisional.

title: A year of business change
finding: VIC records the largest fall: 501 fewer agriculture businesses.
note: Endpoints compare the same agriculture classes. Small changes may reflect confidentiality adjustments, not real entries or exits.

title: Victoria accounts for most of the decline
finding: Victoria accounts for 508 of the 648 fewer registered dairy farms.
note: Floating bars subtract each state’s contribution. This is an accounting comparison, not an explanation of why farms left. End year provisional.

title: Farmers are concentrated in older age groups
finding: An estimated 59% of Farmers and Farm Managers are aged 55+.
note: Same colour, labelled sides. Values are survey estimates in thousands. “Farmer” is an occupation, not everyone working in agriculture. Source sex categories are retained.

title: Business staffing differs between states
finding: Dairy’s non-employing share spans about 48–78% across eligible states.
note: The box holds the middle half of state shares; its line is the median. Each state counts equally. Include ≥100 businesses and ≥5 eligible states per sector. Owners and family may still work.

title: Sheep, beef and grain dominate business numbers
kicker: A DIFFERENT MIX IN EVERY STATE
finding: Sheep, beef cattle and grain account for 70.4% of national agriculture-business class totals.
note: Darker means a larger share, not more workers or revenue. Each state column adds to 100% using the displayed agriculture groups.

title: Business size depends on the sector
finding: About 60% of poultry businesses report annual turnover of at least AUD 200,000.
note: Turnover is sales before expenses, not profit. Percentages use displayed size-bin sums; confidentiality adjustments can make these differ from published totals.

title: Victoria reshapes the dairy map
finding: Victoria holds 65.6% of Australia’s registered dairy farms.
note: State silhouettes are resized so area shows registered farms, not land. Equal-area source shapes are repositioned for legibility. Grey NT/ACT shapes mean not reported and are not count-scaled.

title: Most businesses have no employees
finding: About 75.6% of the derived agriculture-business total is non-employing.
note: Owners and family may still work. Rectangle area shows size-bin counts. Tiny groups are named in the data table. Bin sum 144,678, versus published-class total sum 144,681: the difference reflects confidentiality adjustments.

title: Agriculture’s workforce has become smaller
finding: The annual average fell from 375,000 in 2000 to 247,000 in 2025.
note: Thin line: original quarterly estimates. Thick line: complete-year averages. Latest quarter: about 245,900 in February 2026. This counts the agriculture industry, not just the farmer occupation.
